title: Make study selectable and let it read firstmate at a pinned SHA
summary: Add a [capabilities.study] section to athena.toml so the reader's catalog and schema offer `study`. Add Rust code that checks out https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate read-only at a full 40-character SHA, which is firstmate's main head resolved at study time and recorded. Running firstmate stays out of scope.

defaults_applied.how: The materialiser and tests are Rust; the only non-Rust edits are TOML and Markdown.
New tests cover the catalog and the SHA pin.
The full-SHA pin is enforced in code, not prose.
Prefer the git CLI or an existing crate for fetching over a custom implementation.
Only the public repository URL and a SHA are committed.
One focused change: enable study and add the pinned read.

assumptions: The SHA is resolved from firstmate's current main by a one-time lookup recorded in config. Athena code then enforces the full 40-character SHA at read time. If the producer cannot reach the network, the SHA is left to the user and the code still enforces the pin.
The existing athena-cap-study crate already registers Study in wiring.rs, so the work is config plus a small materialisation module, not a new capability.
Materialisation uses the git CLI or an existing crate, per buy-first, and the choice is recorded.
Tests use a local fixture repository, never the network.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml has a [capabilities.study] section (producer_commands, verifier_commands, env, checks) and is named as a governance edit; [capabilities.change] is unchanged. The verifier grant has no write commands.

Run `cargo test --locked`: a new test loads the repository's athena.toml and shows the reader's catalog offers both `change` and `study` and the reader schema's capability enum is ["change","study",null].

Config records the study source as https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate plus a full 40-character SHA. The SHA is firstmate's main head as resolved at study time and recorded in the config and CHANGELOG. A short, abbreviated, or missing SHA is rejected.
Run `cargo test --locked`: tests using a local fixture git repository (no network) show the source is materialised at exactly the pinned SHA, and a missing, short, or non-matching SHA is an error.
The fetch and checkout happen in Athena's Rust code, not through an agent command. The studied tree is read-only to agents, and the study grants add no network command.
The study card, CHANGELOG.md, and docs/decisions.md (a new D-entry listing alternatives) record the call and say running firstmate remains out of scope.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: both are clean.

out_of_scope: Changes to the study model or records format beyond the source pin
departures: The job touches a governance file and adds new Rust code with fixture-repo tests, so cost and time sit above the reference. The SHA lookup also needs network access, which adds risk.
